response.answer: IMPORTANT CLARIFICATION: The product query references "Lib Tech Skunk Ape 2027." Based on research, the Skunk Ape line for model year 2027 (season 2026-2027) introduced a new variant called the Skunk Ape Twin (True Twin, Camber profile). The merchant-provided attributes (C2x Directional, directional twin shape) match the Skunk Ape C2X which is the 2025-2026 model year (sometimes sold in 2027 calendar year). I will provide facts for both, but the merchant data most closely matches the C2X variant. Where there are disagreements between sources, I flag them explicitly. 1. Brand: Lib Tech [1][2] 2. Model name: Skunk Ape (with variants: Skunk Ape C2X, Skunk Ape Camber, Skunk Ape Twin) [1][2][3] 3. Manufacturer: Mervin Manufacturing [4][5] 4. Mervin Manufacturing was founded by snow/skate/surf enthusiasts Mike Olson and Pete Saari in 1977. 5. Based out of Sequim, Washington, on the Strait of Juan De Fuca between the rugged Olympic and Cascade Mountain Ranges. 6. Manufacturing location: Handbuilt in USA [6] 7. Mervin is the longest running and last major board factory in the USA. 8. Factory address: 65 Banana Way, Sequim, WA 98382 [7] 9. Mervin Manufacturing has been acquired by Spring Capital Group, an Oregon-based private investment firm. 10. Parent company history: Mervin was purchased by Quiksilver in 1997 and later sold to Altamont Capital in 2013. 11. Skunk Ape model first available: approximately 2007/2008 season (earliest catalog entry found is 2008/2009 on SnowDB) [10] 12. Visualized, designed and tested by the man-sized Onion boys Trevor and Kyle Phillips and some select Summit based E-WA consultants, these big wide boards are the ultimate twin freestyle board for the larger footprint. 13. The Skunk Ape C2X directional twin is the 2025-2026 model year (currently on sale) [1] 14. The Skunk Ape Twin (True Twin) is the 2026-2027 model year (new for this season) [3] 15. ALL MOUNTAIN - TRUE TWIN — the 2027 Skunk Ape Twin is a True Twin shape [3] 16. ALL MOUNTAIN - DIRECTIONAL TWIN — the 2026 Skunk Ape C2X is a Directional Twin [1] 17. The Skunk Ape Camber was first introduced for the 2024-2025 season [12] 18. Lib Tech 2025 Skunk Ape Camber Snowboard Review - No Changes For 2026 (the Camber variant was unchanged for 2026) [13] 19. Lib-tech.com user rating (Skunk Ape C2X): 99% of 100 based on 82 reviews [1] 139. Lib-tech.com user rating (Skunk Ape Camber): 98% of 100 based on 19 reviews [27] 140. Lib-tech.com user rating (Skunk Ape Twin): 100% of 100 based on 2 reviews [3] 141. Edge hold: Holds an edge super well and grips well in hard to icy snow. 142. Edge hold negative: It can grab pretty hard in softer snow. 143. With aggressive Magne-Traction edges and camber, this board is an East Coast and ice specialist. Tremendous grip and edge hold make it unbeatable on firm conditions. 144. Carving (C2X): The extra edge hold grips well and allows the Lib-Tech Skunk Ape to carve harder in all conditions but it is not going to be a powerful dynamic carver like a C3 board is. Still, it's pretty good for hybrid rocker. 145. Carving (Camber): Within a few turns I felt at home on this board. Carving on the Skunk Ape was really fun! 146. Speed: Pretty stable and fast for a hybrid rocker board. 147. Base glide concern: This is a board with a thirsty base. It takes a lot of waxing to keep the optimal glide. 148. These Lib Tech boards have a little bit of texture on the base, so they require frequent waxing. But when you do wax them properly, and often they have as good a glide as anybody else in the industry. 149. Uneven terrain (Camber): It blasts through chunder and uneven terrain like a tank. Compared to the rocker version, which can feel twitchy, this one stays stable and damp. 150. Pop/jumps: There is really good pop to it and it's a good choice for air on the mountain as well as in the park. 151. Park performance (Camber): It's surprisingly poppy for its size, popping ollies and butters with ease. 152. Switch riding (C2X): Less as good as the older model but still very doable. 153. Switch riding (Twin): For switch this board is awesome. Set your feet up duck, same angles, and you will have no issue. This is a true twin made to ride switch. 154. Powder float (C2X): The Skunk Ape with the C2 profile noticeably had the edge when I jumped off the piste into the fresh snow. 155. Powder float (Camber): Powder float isn't its strongest area, but for a full camber board with limited setback, it performs better than expected. 156. Whitelines tester verdict: I was blown away by the regular Skunk Ape snowboard... was surprisingly quick edge to edge despite its size and had phenomenal grip for carving. 157. Durability: This board is going to be a tank. The skunk apes in the past are all juggernauts. This thing's made to be ridden by big guys, and it's built like that. 158. Dampening: For the uneven snow, this board is going to handle tracked out snow with ease. The construction on these skunk apes absorb chatter. They don't give you a lot of feedback. 159. This is the new twin version of the Skunk ape that came previously in a directional camber and rocker model. This has a less aggressive, more forgiving, more playful personality. 160. This is a much more everyday rider friendly type of ride. 161. If you are somebody looking for a super hard charger like the other Skunk Apes, and you get this expecting it to be a hard charger, you might be a little disappointed. 162. This board is a fun ass, mountain freestyle ride. 163. Only available in Wide (no Ultra Wide), only two sizes (163W, 166W) [3] 164. The turn initiation with this board is medium fast, edge to edge. 165. Very enjoyable carving experience where you can lay a trench, come across the groomer and boost out of it going faster than you came into it. 166. Width makes edge-to-edge slower: Edge changes aren't as quick, for obvious reasons, so that's something that requires getting used to. 167. Slow speed handling: Even with the combo profile it's tricky to mess around with at slower speeds. 168. Weight concern for larger boards: It's not the lightest or most nimble board. 169. Lib Tech Boards in general run on the sturdy/heavy side so this isn't going to be one of those ultra-light boards. 170. Too wide for smaller-footed riders: If you aren't a bigger footed rider... this is going to be hard to skid turns. 171. Forum user concern: I'm not used to riding anything this stiff, but I'm also wondering if I tried to get too wide a board for no reason. 172. Bigger boards heavy on chairlifts: Not too wide, but a board that big will be heavy hanging off one leg on the chair. 173.
